mechanism: Betamethasone increases renal potassium wasting and sodium retention while furosemide causes significant electrolyte depletion, leading to synergistic hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and alkalosis; both drugs also increase cardiac arrhythmia risk and glucocorticoids can impair renal function.
action: Monitor serum electrolytes (especially potassium), renal function, and blood pressure regularly; consider potassium supplementation or concurrent potassium-sparing agent; assess for signs of hypokalemia and cardiac arrhythmias.
